title: Lapidary’s fingers
html_source: Stephen watches from the window in front of the shop of Thomas Russell, lapidary and gem cutter, 57 Fleet Street. The name “Russell” likely has him thinking of what he considers a fiasco in his attempts to engage those in the National Library, including George Russell (AE). The language in this passage, especially a reference to “fallen archangels” suggests an attitude of abject defeat in Stephen. There are allusions to Bloom’s paternal sense of defeat here, as well. Bloom as modern-day Ulysses (sailorman), Molly flapping (flaunting) a ruby egg on her gross belly.
